ConocoPhillips fell 0.45% today to $126.73, extending a weak two-week stretch down 7.27%. The stock has been pressured by escalating U.S.-Iran tensions and the prospect of a domestic diesel export ban—both factors that create uncertainty for a major oil producer and refiner. A potential export ban on diesel would constrain U.S. refiner profits (refiners profit from the spread between crude input costs and refined product prices), while heightened geopolitical risk around Iran could tighten global oil supplies, pushing prices higher in ways that may take time to benefit producers or that markets are already pricing in.

The wider context is a divergence between U.S. and world oil prices: crude is trading at $96.41 per barrel domestically but $114.89 globally, suggesting the market is pricing in both supply uncertainty abroad and tighter margins at home if export restrictions take hold. This kind of policy-driven volatility—where government action constrains the upside even as geopolitical risk should support prices—tends to keep energy stocks on the defensive until the rules become clearer.
